newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela sends warm message to Kabila.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela sends warm message to Kabila.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela did not attend Laurent Kabila's inauguration as the new President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, but sent a warm message of congratulations, a spokesman said on Thursday.
Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said no slight was intended by the low level of South Africa's representation at the ceremony in Kinshasa.
"The president sent a special message to Mr Kabila, a very warm message of support," Mankahlana said.
Mandela has said repeatedly that he has absolute confidence in Kabila to bring democracy to his country. On Tuesday he accused the West of demonising the former rebel leader.
Officials said Mandela had planned to send Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, who played a key role in his seven-month effort to negotiate a peaceful transition to democracy in the former Zaire.
But Mandela, fearing that his deputy, who acts as prime minister, was nearing exhaustion, instructed Mbeki at the weekend to cancel his programme for the next two weeks and take a vacation.
Officials insist Mbeki is in good health and only needs a break from his gruelling schedule.
"The decision to send Mr Mbeki on holiday was taken at very short notice and the president was unable to rearrange his diary in the time available," Mankahlana said.
Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo was already committed to the ministers' preparatory meeting for the Organisation of African Unity summit in Harare next week.
In the event South Africa was reperesented only by its ambassador to the Democratic Republic of Congo Jan van Deventer.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Pieter Swanepoel said Mandela had signalled his support for Kabila's administration by sending Mbeki to meet Kabila immediately after he proclaimed himself president. "That was a very strong symbolic gesture," he said.
Mankahlana said Mandela would meet Kabila privately at the OAU summit and reaffirmed that South Africa would cooperate with the Kinshasa government to rebuild the country and create sound government.
